item.title: Controlling C/C++ Structure Alignment with #pragma pack
item.description:
“Controlling C/C++ Structure Alignment with #pragma pack”

The #pragma pack directive serves as a mechanism to issue compiler-specific instructions, primarily to dictate the memory alignment boundary for structure members. By default, compilers often insert padding bytes between structure elements to ensure members align on addresses that are multiples of their respective sizes (e.g., 4-byte integers aligning on 4-byte boundaries). This default alignment typically maximizes memory access speed on the target architecture. However, scenarios exist where this default behavior must be overridden.
